textbookText: 21. The dimension of Planck's constant (h) is the same as that of: A) Angular momentum B) Energy C) Force D) Power
22. Which of the following has 1 significant figure? A) 0.007 B) 700 C) 7.00 D) 7.0 × 10²

23. A student records g = 9.8 m/s² instead of the true 9.81 m/s². This is an example of: A) An error affecting accuracy (systematic/rounding limitation) B) A precision-only error with no effect on accuracy C) A gross blunder in reading the scale D) An error caused by parallax alone
24. Dimensional formula of universal gravitational constant G is: A) [M⁻¹L³T⁻²] B) [MLT⁻²] C) [ML²T⁻²] D) [ML⁻¹T⁻²]
25. Which of these quantities is a "supplementary" unit in SI (not base, not derived)? A) Radian (plane angle) B) Kelvin (temperature) C) Mole (amount of substance) D) Ampere (current)

26. The least count of a vernier caliper is generally: A) 0.01 cm — smaller than that of a metre scale (0.1 cm) B) 0.1 cm — same as a metre scale C) 1 cm — larger than a metre scale D) 0.001 mm — same as a screw gauge
27. A number expressed as 3.40 × 10⁵ has: A) 3 significant figures B) 5 significant figures C) 6 significant figures D) 1 significant figure

28. Which of the following relations is dimensionally WRONG? A) Time period T = 2π√(l/g) for a pendulum B) Kinetic energy = ½mv² C) Force = mass × velocity (claiming this equals mass × acceleration) D) Pressure = Force/Area

29. The percentage error is defined as: A) (Absolute error / True or mean value) × 100% B) (True value / Absolute error) × 100% C) Absolute error alone, without reference to true value D) The number of significant figures × 10%

30. Why is significant-figure reporting important in scientific data (e.g., in Pioneer Physics lab work)? A) It communicates the precision/reliability of a measurement honestly B) It makes numbers look shorter for convenience only C) It is required only for very large numbers, not small ones D) It has no real scientific purpose, only a formatting convention
